tsv-s01-v01.label: stanza-1
cite_parts: यदयमनुत्तरमूर्तिर्नजेच्छयाखिलमिदं जगत्स्रष्टुम्। पस्पन्दे स स्पन्दः प्रथमः शिवतत्त्वमुच्यते तज्ज्ञैः॥१॥
tsv-s01-v01.quick_english: That Anuttara-formed one, by his own desire to manifest all this world, vibrated; that first vibration is called the Śiva-principle by those who know it.

tsv-s01-v02.label: stanza-2
cite_parts: इच्छा सैव स्वच्छा सन्ततसमवायिनी सती शक्तिः। सचराचरस्य जगतो बीजं निखिलस्य निजनिलीनस्य॥२॥
tsv-s01-v02.quick_english: Will itself — transparent, ever-co-inherent, being — is power: the seed of the entire world of moving and unmoving things, hidden in herself.

tsv-s01-v03.label: stanza-3
cite_parts: स्वेच्छाशक्त्युद्गीर्णं जगदात्मतया समाच्छाद्य। निवसन् स एव निखिलानुग्रहनिरतः सदाशिवोऽभिहितः॥३॥
tsv-s01-v03.quick_english: Having fully covered with the Self the world emitted by own will-power, abiding — he indeed, devoted to all grace, is called Sadāśiva.

tokens.grounds: abhihita ppp with elision, called Sadāśiva

tsv-s01-v04.label: stanza-4
cite_parts: विश्वं पश्चात्पश्यनिदन्तया निखिलमीश्वरो जातः। सा भवति शुद्धविद्या येदन्ताहन्तयोरभेदमतिः॥४॥
tsv-s01-v04.quick_english: Seeing the universe after himself with this-ness, the Lord has become all; that becomes pure knowledge, in which this and I are held non-different.

tokens.grounds: paśyan with paścāt and idantā instrumental

tsv-s01-v05.label: stanza-5
cite_parts: माया विभेदबुद्धिर्निजांशजातेषु निखिलजीवेषु। नित्यं तस्य निरङ्कुशविभवं वेलेव वारिधे रुन्धे॥५॥
tsv-s01-v05.quick_english: Māyā is difference-notion toward all beings born of own portions; always his unbridled power — like the ocean shore — blocks.

tokens.grounds: vibhedabuddhi with the compound locative plural

tsv-s01-v06.label: stanza-6
cite_parts: स तया परिमितमूर्तिः सङ्कुचितसमस्तशक्तिरेष पुमान्। रविरिव सन्ध्यारक्तः संहृतशक्तिः स्वभासनेऽप्यपटुः॥६॥
tsv-s01-v06.quick_english: He, by her, of limited form with all powers contracted — this is the Person; like the sun red at dusk, powers withdrawn, unskilled even in self-shining.

tokens.grounds: apaṭu with sva-bhāsana and api nominative

tsv-s01-v07.label: stanza-7
cite_parts: सम्पूर्णकर्तृताद्या बह्व्यः सन्त्यस्य शक्तयस्तस्य। सङ्कोचात्सङ्कुचिताः कलादिरूपेण रूढयन्त्येवम्॥७॥
tsv-s01-v07.quick_english: Complete doership and the rest — many are his powers; through contraction contracted, in the form of kalā and the rest, thus they ascend.

tokens.grounds: with elision 3pl of as with genitive
visarga to s before t feminine nominative plural

tsv-s01-v08.label: stanza-8
cite_parts: तत्सर्वकर्तृता सा सङ्कुचिता कतिपयार्थमात्रपरा। किञ्चित्कर्तारममुं कलयन्ती कीर्त्यते कला नाम॥८॥
tsv-s01-v08.quick_english: That all-doership, contracted, directed merely at a few things — making him a doer-of-little — is called kalā by name.

tsv-s01-v09.label: stanza-9
cite_parts: सर्वज्ञतास्य शक्तिः परिमिततनुरल्पवेद्यमात्रपरा। ज्ञानमुत्पादयन्ती विद्येति निगद्यते बुधैराद्यैः॥९॥
tsv-s01-v09.quick_english: His all-knowing power, of limited body, directed merely at little to be known — producing knowledge — is declared vidyā by the ancient wise.

tokens.grounds: para with the long compound nominative

tsv-s01-v10.label: stanza-10
cite_parts: नित्यपरिपूर्णतृप्तिः शक्तिस्तस्यैव परिमिता तु सती। भोगेषु रञ्जयन्ती सततममुं रागतत्त्वतां याता॥१०॥
tsv-s01-v10.quick_english: Ever-full satisfaction, his very power, yet limited, being — ever coloring him toward enjoyments — has become raga-principle-ness.

tokens.grounds: visarga to s before t feminine

tsv-s01-v11.label: stanza-11
cite_parts: सा नित्यतास्य शक्तिर्निकृष्य निधनोदयप्रदानेन। नियतपरिच्छेदकरी कॢप्ता स्यात्कालतत्त्वरूपेण॥११॥
tsv-s01-v11.quick_english: That eternity, his power — having drawn off by giving rise-and-fall — making fixed divisions, is arranged in the form of the time-principle.

tsv-s01-v12.label: stanza-12
cite_parts: यास्य स्वतन्त्रताख्या शक्तिः सङ्कोचशालिनी सैव। कृत्याकृत्येष्ववशं नियतममुं नियमयन्त्यभून्नियतिः॥१२॥
tsv-s01-v12.quick_english: Which power of his called autonomy, rich in contraction — that very one, constraining him helplessly fixed in do-and-do-not, became restriction.

tokens.grounds: avaśa with the dvandva locative plural
niyamayantī with abhūt and niyatiḥ nominative

tsv-s01-v13.label: stanza-13
cite_parts: इच्छादित्रिसमष्टिः शक्तिः शान्तास्य सङ्कुचद्रूपा। सङ्कलितेच्छाद्यात्मकसत्त्वादिकसाम्यरूपिणी तु सती॥१३॥
tsv-s01-v13.quick_english: The triad-collection of will and the rest — power, quiescent, of contracted form in him; but consisting, being, in the sameness of sattva and the rest whose nature is collected will and the rest.

tsv-s01-v14.label: stanza-14
cite_parts: बुद्ध्यादिसामरस्यस्वरूपचित्तात्मिका मता प्रकृतिः। इच्छास्य रजोरूपाहङ्कृतिरासीदहम्प्रतीतिकरी॥१४॥
tsv-s01-v14.quick_english: Deemed prakṛti: of the nature of citta whose nature is the fusion of buddhi and the rest; his will, as rajas-formed I-making effecting I-notion, was.

tsv-s01-v15.label: stanza-15
cite_parts: ज्ञानापि सत्त्वरूपा निर्णयबोधस्य कारणं बुद्धिः। तस्य क्रिया तमोमयमूर्तिर्मन उच्यते विकल्पकरी॥१५॥
tsv-s01-v15.quick_english: Even knowledge, of sattva-nature, is the cause of determinative cognition — buddhi; its action, dark-formed-bodied, is called mind, the doubting-maker.

tsv-s01-v16.label: stanza-16
cite_parts: वामादिपञ्चभेदः स एव सङ्कुचितविग्रहो देवः। ज्ञानक्रियोपरागप्राधान्याद्विविधविषयरूपोऽभूत्॥१६॥
tsv-s01-v16.quick_english: With fivefold division beginning with Vāmā, that very god of contracted body — through knowledge-action-tinge predominance became of manifold-object form.

tsv-s01-v17.label: stanza-17
cite_parts: श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनजिह्वाघ्राणानि बोधकरणानि। शब्दस्पर्शौ रूपं रसगन्धौ चेति भूतसूक्ष्माणि॥१७॥
tsv-s01-v17.quick_english: Ear, eye, touch, tongue, nose are the knowledge-instruments; sound, touch, form, taste, smell — thus the subtle elements.

tsv-s01-v18.label: stanza-18
cite_parts: अयमेवातिनिकृष्टो जातो भूतात्मनापि भूतेशः। गगनमनिलश्च तेजः सलिलं भूमिश्च पञ्चभूतानि॥१८॥
tsv-s01-v18.quick_english: This very one, most base-born, even as elemental self, is the Lord of beings; ether, air, fire, water, earth — the five gross elements.

tokens.grounds: aya with eva and atinikṛṣṭa nominative

tsv-s01-v19.label: stanza-19
cite_parts: श्रोत्रादिकरणवेद्याः शब्दाद्यास्तानि वेदकान्येषाम्। वचनकरी वागासीत् पाणिः स्यात्करणभूत आदाने॥१९॥
tsv-s01-v19.quick_english: Beginning with sound, to be known by ear and other instruments — they are the knowns of these; speech was the uttering-maker, the hand would be the instrument-being in taking.

tokens.grounds: vedya with the compound nominative plural
ādi with śabda nominative plural apposition

tsv-s01-v20.label: stanza-20
cite_parts: गमनविसर्गानन्दत्रितये पादादिकं करणम्। गन्धवती भूमिः स्यादापः सांसिद्धिकद्रवास्तेजः॥२०॥
tsv-s01-v20.quick_english: In the triad of going, excreting, bliss — foot and the rest as instrument; earth would be smell-possessing, waters naturally fluid, fire.

tsv-s01-v21.label: stanza-21
cite_parts: उष्णस्पर्शमरूपस्पर्शो वायुरम्बरं सशब्दम्। षट्त्रिंशत्तत्त्वमयं वन्दे कौलं कुलातिगं शम्भुम्॥२१॥
tsv-s01-v21.quick_english: Hot touch and formless touch is wind; ether with sound. I praise the Kaula consisting of thirty-six principles, beyond the kula — Śambhu.

tsv-s01-v01.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v01.question: What vibrated to manifest the world, and what is the first vibration called?
premises: That Anuttara-formed one, by own desire, willed to manifest all this world.
It vibrated, and that first vibration is called the Śiva-principle by its knowers.
tsv-s01-v01.inference: Self-willed vibration of the Highest is the first Śiva-tattva.
uncertainties: Desire-to-manifest object carried into the infinitive.

tsv-s01-v02.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v02.question: What is Śakti as seed of the world?
premises: Will itself, transparent, ever-co-inherent, being — is power.
She is the seed of the entire moving-and-unmoving world hidden in herself.
tsv-s01-v02.inference: Transparent ever-present will-power seeds the self-hidden world.

tsv-s01-v03.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v03.question: Who is called Sadāśiva, abiding devoted to all grace?
premises: Having covered the will-emitted world with the Self, abiding.
He indeed, devoted to all grace, is called Sadāśiva.
tsv-s01-v03.inference: Self-covering abiding in all-grace is Sadāśiva.
uncertainties: Covering agency, his own act presumed.

tsv-s01-v04.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v04.question: How does the Lord become all, and what is pure knowledge?
premises: Seeing the universe after himself with this-ness, the Lord has become all.
That becomes pure knowledge, in which this and I are held non-different.
tsv-s01-v04.inference: All-become Lordship yields pure knowledge of this-I non-difference.

tsv-s01-v05.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v05.question: What does Māyā do to all beings, and what blocks like the shore?
premises: Māyā is difference-notion toward all beings born of own portions.
Always his unbridled power, like the ocean shore, blocks.
tsv-s01-v05.inference: Māyā differentiates own-portion beings while unbridled power shore-blocks.

tsv-s01-v06.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v06.question: Who is the Person of contracted powers?
premises: He, by her, of limited form with all powers contracted — this is the Person.
Like the dusk-red sun, powers withdrawn, unskilled even in self-shining.
tsv-s01-v06.inference: Her contraction makes the limited Person, dusk-sun-like, dim even to himself.

tsv-s01-v07.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v07.question: How do his many powers ascend in kalā-form?
premises: Complete doership and the rest — many are his powers.
Through contraction contracted, in kalā-and-rest form, thus they make ascend.
tsv-s01-v07.inference: Many powers, contracted into kalā-forms, ascend.

tsv-s01-v08.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v08.question: What is called kalā?
premises: That all-doership, contracted, directed merely at a few things.
Making him a doer-of-little, it is called kalā by name.
tsv-s01-v08.inference: Contracted all-doership directed at few things is kalā.

tsv-s01-v09.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v09.question: What is declared vidyā by the ancient wise?
premises: His all-knowing power, of limited body, directed merely at little to be known.
Producing knowledge, it is declared vidyā by the ancient wise.
tsv-s01-v09.inference: Limited all-knowing power producing knowledge is vidyā.

tsv-s01-v10.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v10.question: How has satisfaction become raga-tattva?
premises: Ever-full satisfaction, his very power, yet limited, being.
Ever coloring him toward enjoyments, it has become raga-principle-ness.
tsv-s01-v10.inference: Limited ever-satisfaction coloring him toward enjoyments is raga.

tsv-s01-v11.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v11.question: How is eternity arranged as the time-principle?
premises: That eternity, his power, having drawn off by giving rise-and-fall.
Making fixed divisions, it is arranged, in time-principle form.
tsv-s01-v11.inference: Eternity drawn off through rise-and-fall fixes divisions as time.

tsv-s01-v12.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v12.question: How did autonomy-power become restriction?
premises: Which power of his called autonomy, rich in contraction — that very one.
Constraining him helplessly fixed in do-and-do-not, it became restriction.
tsv-s01-v12.inference: Autonomy-power contracting into do-don’t constraint is niyati.

tsv-s01-v13.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v13.question: What is the quiescent collected power of sameness?
premises: The triad-collection of will and the rest — power, quiescent, of contracted form in him.
But consisting in the sameness of sattva and the rest whose nature is collected will and the rest, being.
tsv-s01-v13.inference: Collected will-powers rest contracted in guṇa-sameness.

tsv-s01-v14.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v14.question: What is deemed prakṛti, and what was his will as I-making?
premises: Deemed prakṛti: of the nature of citta whose nature is the fusion of buddhi and the rest.
His will, as rajas-formed I-making effecting I-notion, was.
tsv-s01-v14.inference: Fusion-natured citta is prakṛti, and his will was the I-notion-effecting rajas I-making.

tsv-s01-v15.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v15.question: What are buddhi and mind?
premises: Even knowledge, of sattva-nature, is the cause of determinative cognition — buddhi.
Its action, dark-formed-bodied, is called mind, the doubting-maker.
tsv-s01-v15.inference: Sattvic determinative cause is buddhi, while its dark active body doubting is mind.

tsv-s01-v16.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v16.question: How did the contracted-bodied god become manifold objects?
premises: With fivefold division beginning with Vāmā, that very god of contracted body.
Through knowledge-action-tinge predominance became of manifold-object form.
tsv-s01-v16.inference: The five-divided contracted god objectifies manifoldly via knowledge-action tinge.

tsv-s01-v17.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v17.question: Which are the knowledge-instruments and subtle elements?
premises: Ear, eye, touch, tongue, nose are the knowledge-instruments.
Sound, touch, form, taste, smell — thus the subtle elements.
tsv-s01-v17.inference: Five know-organs pair with five subtle elements.

tsv-s01-v18.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v18.question: Who is Lord of beings even as elemental self, and what are the five gross?
premises: This very one, most base-born, even as elemental self, is the Lord of beings.
Ether, air, fire, water, earth — the five gross elements.
tsv-s01-v18.inference: The base-born elemental self is beings-Lord over the five gross.

tsv-s01-v19.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v19.question: What do ear-instruments know, and what are speech and hand?
premises: Beginning with sound, to be known by ear and other instruments — they are the knowns of these.
Speech was the uttering-maker; the hand would be the instrument-being in taking.
tsv-s01-v19.inference: Knowns pair with knowers while speech utters and hand takes.

tsv-s01-v20.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v20.question: What are foot function and earth-water-fire qualities?
premises: In the triad of going, excreting, bliss — foot and the rest as instrument.
Earth would be smell-possessing; waters naturally fluid; fire.
tsv-s01-v20.inference: Foot serves the action-triad while earth-water-fire carry smell-fluidity-heat.
uncertainties: Fire quality carried from the next verse.

tsv-s01-v21.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
tsv-s01-v21.question: What are wind-ether touches, and whom does the poet praise?
premises: Hot touch and formless touch is wind; ether with sound.
I praise the Kaula consisting of thirty-six principles, beyond the kula — Śambhu.
tsv-s01-v21.inference: Wind-ether complete the elements, and the poet praises the thirty-six-principled beyond-kula Śambhu.

tsv-s01-v06.sanskrit_cite: स तया परिमितमूर्तिः सङ्कुचितसमस्तशक्तिरेष पुमान्। रविरिव सन्ध्यारक्तः संहृतशक्तिः स्वभासनेऽप्यपटुः॥६॥

tsv-s01-v07.plain_english: Complete doership and the rest — many are his powers; through contraction contracted, in the form of kalā and the rest, thus they ascend.
tsv-s01-v07.sanskrit_cite: सम्पूर्णकर्तृताद्या बह्व्यः सन्त्यस्य शक्तयस्तस्य। सङ्कोचात्सङ्कुचिताः कलादिरूपेण रूढयन्त्येवम्॥७॥

tsv-s01-v08.plain_english: That all-doership, contracted, directed merely at a few things — making him a doer-of-little — is called kalā by name.
tsv-s01-v08.sanskrit_cite: तत्सर्वकर्तृता सा सङ्कुचिता कतिपयार्थमात्रपरा। किञ्चित्कर्तारममुं कलयन्ती कीर्त्यते कला नाम॥८॥

tsv-s01-v09.plain_english: His all-knowing power, of limited body, directed merely at little to be known — producing knowledge — is declared vidyā by the ancient wise.
tsv-s01-v09.sanskrit_cite: सर्वज्ञतास्य शक्तिः परिमिततनुरल्पवेद्यमात्रपरा। ज्ञानमुत्पादयन्ती विद्येति निगद्यते बुधैराद्यैः॥९॥

tsv-s01-v10.plain_english: Ever-full satisfaction, his very power, yet limited, being — ever coloring him toward enjoyments — has become raga-principle-ness.
tsv-s01-v10.sanskrit_cite: नित्यपरिपूर्णतृप्तिः शक्तिस्तस्यैव परिमिता तु सती। भोगेषु रञ्जयन्ती सततममुं रागतत्त्वतां याता॥१०॥

tsv-s01-v11.plain_english: That eternity, his power — having drawn off by giving rise-and-fall — making fixed divisions, is arranged in the form of the time-principle.
tsv-s01-v11.sanskrit_cite: सा नित्यतास्य शक्तिर्निकृष्य निधनोदयप्रदानेन। नियतपरिच्छेदकरी कॢप्ता स्यात्कालतत्त्वरूपेण॥११॥

tsv-s01-v12.plain_english: Which power of his called autonomy, rich in contraction — that very one, constraining him helplessly fixed in do-and-do-not, became restriction.
tsv-s01-v12.sanskrit_cite: यास्य स्वतन्त्रताख्या शक्तिः सङ्कोचशालिनी सैव। कृत्याकृत्येष्ववशं नियतममुं नियमयन्त्यभून्नियतिः॥१२॥

tsv-s01-v13.plain_english: The triad-collection of will and the rest — power, quiescent, of contracted form in him; but consisting, being, in the sameness of sattva and the rest whose nature is collected will and the rest.
tsv-s01-v13.sanskrit_cite: इच्छादित्रिसमष्टिः शक्तिः शान्तास्य सङ्कुचद्रूपा। सङ्कलितेच्छाद्यात्मकसत्त्वादिकसाम्यरूपिणी तु सती॥१३॥

tsv-s01-v14.plain_english: Deemed prakṛti: of the nature of citta whose nature is the fusion of buddhi and the rest; his will, as rajas-formed I-making effecting I-notion, was.

tsv-s01-v15.plain_english: Even knowledge, of sattva-nature, is the cause of determinative cognition — buddhi; its action, dark-formed-bodied, is called mind, the doubting-maker.
tsv-s01-v15.sanskrit_cite: ज्ञानापि सत्त्वरूपा निर्णयबोधस्य कारणं बुद्धिः। तस्य क्रिया तमोमयमूर्तिर्मन उच्यते विकल्पकरी॥१५॥

tsv-s01-v16.plain_english: With fivefold division beginning with Vāmā, that very god of contracted body — through knowledge-action-tinge predominance became of manifold-object form.

tsv-s01-v17.plain_english: Ear, eye, touch, tongue, nose are the knowledge-instruments; sound, touch, form, taste, smell — thus the subtle elements.
tsv-s01-v17.sanskrit_cite: श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनजिह्वाघ्राणानि बोधकरणानि। शब्दस्पर्शौ रूपं रसगन्धौ चेति भूतसूक्ष्माणि॥१७॥

tsv-s01-v18.plain_english: This very one, most base-born, even as elemental self, is the Lord of beings; ether, air, fire, water, earth — the five gross elements.
tsv-s01-v18.sanskrit_cite: अयमेवातिनिकृष्टो जातो भूतात्मनापि भूतेशः। गगनमनिलश्च तेजः सलिलं भूमिश्च पञ्चभूतानि॥१८॥

tsv-s01-v19.plain_english: Beginning with sound, to be known by ear and other instruments — they are the knowns of these; speech was the uttering-maker, the hand would be the instrument-being in taking.
tsv-s01-v19.sanskrit_cite: श्रोत्रादिकरणवेद्याः शब्दाद्यास्तानि वेदकान्येषाम्। वचनकरी वागासीत् पाणिः स्यात्करणभूत आदाने॥१९॥

tsv-s01-v20.plain_english: In the triad of going, excreting, bliss — foot and the rest as instrument; earth would be smell-possessing, waters naturally fluid, fire.
tsv-s01-v20.sanskrit_cite: गमनविसर्गानन्दत्रितये पादादिकं करणम्। गन्धवती भूमिः स्यादापः सांसिद्धिकद्रवास्तेजः॥२०॥

tsv-s01-v21.plain_english: Hot touch and formless touch is wind; ether with sound. I praise the Kaula consisting of thirty-six principles, beyond the kula — Śambhu.
tsv-s01-v21.sanskrit_cite: उष्णस्पर्शमरूपस्पर्शो वायुरम्बरं सशब्दम्। षट्त्रिंशत्तत्त्वमयं वन्दे कौलं कुलातिगं शम्भुम्॥२१॥

essence: Self-willed vibration of the Highest is the first Śiva-tattva.
Transparent ever-present will-power seeds the self-hidden world.
Self-covering abiding in all-grace is Sadāśiva.
All-become Lordship yields pure knowledge of this-I non-difference.
Māyā differentiates own-portion beings while unbridled power shore-blocks.
